prompt_text: Where should I stay in Branson Missouri, an Airbnb or a hotel, and which specific places are best?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer — it depends on what you want to do in Branson:

- Pick a hotel if you want convenience, predictable service, on‑site amenities (desk, daily cleaning, pools, breakfast), and easy walkability to shows/attractions.
- Pick an Airbnb/cabin if you want more space, a kitchen, better per‑person value for families/groups, or lake/cabin privacy.

Which to choose by trip type
- Visiting shows, dining out, nightlife: stay on or very near the 76 “Branson Strip” (Country Boulevard) or Branson Landing — a hotel is usually easiest.
- Going to Silver Dollar City/theme‑park days: stay in Branson/Hollister area or in Branson West so your drive to the park and parking are short.
- Lake/boating/quiet getaway: rent a cabin or condo on/near Table Rock Lake (Indian Point, Hollister, Ridgedale) or book a lakeside resort.
- Large families or groups: a multi‑bedroom cabin or whole‑house Airbnb is often cheaper and more comfortable than several hotel rooms.
- Romantic or luxury stay: go with a resort or high‑end hotel.

Specific properties and types to consider
- Big Cedar Lodge (near Table Rock Lake/Ridgedale) — top choice for upscale, outdoorsy resort experience; lots of on‑site activities and dining. Great for couples/families wanting nature plus amenities.
- Chateau on the Lake Resort Spa & Convention Center — lakefront luxury with spa and fine dining; good for couples/anniversary stays.
- Welk Resort Branson — condo‑style units, family friendly, good for multi‑night family stays.
- Hilton Promenade at Branson Landing — on the Landing with easy walk to shops and restaurants along the waterfront.
- Drury Inn & Suites (Branson area) — reliable mid‑range option with free hot breakfast and evening snacks; convenient for the Strip.
- If budget is priority: well‑reviewed chain hotels (Hampton, Holiday Inn Express, Comfort Suites, La Quinta, Best Western) on/near the Strip often give the best value.

Airbnb tips
- Search for “entire place” cabins or condos if you want privacy/kitchen.
- Favor listings with many recent reviews and “Superhost” status.
- Pay attention to total price (cleaning fee and service fees can add a lot).
- Check parking availability and distance to the Strip or lake; Branson requires a car for many sites unless you stay right on the Landing.
- If you’ll be boating, verify boat parking/dock availability.

Hotel tips
- Look for free parking and breakfast (Drury and many HIs/Hampton Inns do this).
- If you want nightlife and shows, prioritize proximity to 76 Country Boulevard.
- Ask about resort fees, free cancellation, and shuttle availability to shows or the airport.

When to book
- Summer, fall foliage and holiday weekends fill up quickly — book as early as possible.
- If your dates are flexible, mid‑week is cheaper and less crowded.

If you tell me your dates, number of people, budget, and whether you want lake access or to be on the Strip, I can shortlist 4–6 exact hotel or Airbnb options and give estimated prices.
